census_method: GitHub code search on 6 exact strings (see ../research-log.md 1.4), plus the CrossPoint/FreeInk repo sets carried over from the 2026-09-04 sweep.
caveat: No example in this catalogue has been built or run by this repository. No X4 Classic hardware was available. Every 'status' below is the upstream author's own claim or a dated community report, never a local result.

examples.title: FreeInk SDK reference build, env x4c
examples.author: Free-Ink
examples.toolchain: PlatformIO + Arduino-ESP32; exact version not pinned in the sample ini
examples.strengths: The authoritative board profile. Everything else derives from it.
examples.pitfalls: displaySpiHz changed 20 MHz -> 10 MHz at commit 39606d5a (2026-09-09). A build pinned before that clocks the panel twice as fast as upstream now recommends.

examples.title: Draftling writerdeck, board xteink_x4_classic
examples.author: clackups
examples.hardware_status: explicitly NOT tested on X4 Classic hardware; the author says so in HARDWARE.md
examples.strengths: A second, independent reading of the board profile written for a different application. Names the X4C/X4 v2 equivalence, the DC/RST/BUSY difference from the X4 Pro, and the reason for a dual-OTA table.
examples.pitfalls: It is a text editor, not a reader. Its display backend runs the panel at the OEM's 5 MHz, not FreeInk's rate. Blind port for this board.

examples.title: CrossPoint Reader, env x4c
examples.author: crosspoint-reader
examples.hardware_status: reported-working - u/Diirge, r/xteinkereader 1wbxvvg comment p8vlefa, 2026-09-10: 'CrossPoint sleep screen rendering got much better as of today on the x4c'
examples.strengths: The firmware most X4C owners will actually run.
examples.pitfalls: No commit pinned this pass - the immutable_url is null and that is a real gap in this catalogue.
examples.lineage: independent reader firmware, uses the FreeInk board data

examples.title: esphome-xteink
examples.author: vjFaLk
examples.pitfalls: Vendors the FreeInk SDK verbatim; not an independent implementation. Its own description names X4/X3/X4 Pro, not the X4C.
examples.selection: REJECTED - duplicate of E01, no X4C-specific content

examples.title: Inkkit shared HAL
examples.author: mohitagw15856
examples.pitfalls: src/BoardConfig.h is a copy. Scoped by its own description to 'Xteink X4/X3, ESP32-C3'.

examples.title: x4pro-emu - QEMU model of the X4 Pro
examples.author: kycube
examples.license: none stated - all rights reserved by default
examples.license_evidence: GitHub reports no licence; no LICENSE file in the tree
examples.hardware_status: n/a - it is an emulator, built against a physical X4 Pro
examples.strengths: Boots both stock 7.2.4 and CrossPoint 1.6.0 to their home screens. Publishes an eFuse dump, a partition decode and register-level traces.
examples.pitfalls: Models the X4 PRO, not the X4 Classic. No radio; WiFi stops itself after ~8 s.
examples.selection: NOT AN X4C EXAMPLE - catalogued because it is the nearest runnable target and because building an X4C variant of it is the cheapest untried way to test X4C firmware

feature_coverage.imu_qmi8658: E01 only - and NOTHING exercises Shake-to-Flip, the vendor's own headline feature
feature_coverage.usb_msc: E01 claims support; no example and no socket
feature_coverage.wifi_ble: E02 (BLE keyboard) - untested on this board

uncovered: QMI8658 motion input / Shake-to-Flip - no example anywhere
USB-MSC - enabled in the SDK, physically awkward, never demonstrated
NVS screenType recovery after an accidental full erase - the board's single worst failure mode has no worked example
